name: mmap2
synopsis: void *syscall(SYS_mmap2, unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, unsigned long prot, unsigned long flags, unsigned long fd, unsigned long pgoffset);
description: The mmap2() system call maps files or devices into memory, similar to mmap(2), but with the offset specified in 4096-byte units to support large files on 32-bit systems. It is typically invoked via the glibc wrapper and is not the primary interface users should use.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address for the memory mapping

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Length of the mapping in bytes

parameters.name: prot
parameters.description: Protection options for the mapped memory

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to map

parameters.name: pgoffset
parameters.description: Offset into the file in 4096-byte units

return_value.success: Returns a pointer to the mapped area
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: Problem with getting the data from user space
Offset multiplied by 4096 is not a multiple of the system page size

bugs: This system call does not exist on x86-64. On ia64, the unit for offset is the system page size rather than 4096 bytes.
